memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They came out with all their troops and a large number of horses and chariots—a huge army, as numerous as the sand on the seashore. All these kings joined forces and made camp together at the Waters of Merom to fight against Israel - Josh 11:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The writer wants us to feel the size of this. Horses, chariots, a coalition of kings, soldiers as countless as sand on the shore. On paper, Israel should lose. They had no chariots to speak of and no cavalry. Everything visible was stacked against them.

We often measure our situations the same way — by what we can count. The bills, the diagnosis, the number of people against us, the years already lost. And when the counting is done, the conclusion feels obvious: there is no way through. The Waters of Merom teach us that God's people are frequently outnumbered on paper long before they are delivered in reality.

But the phrase "as numerous as the sand on the seashore" should catch our ear. That is the very language God used for His promise to Abraham (Gen 22:17). The enemy looks like sand; God had already promised that Abraham's descendants would be like sand. The threat only echoes a promise God made long before the battle began.

Whatever looks countless and overwhelming in front of you today, remember that God is not intimidated by large numbers. He has a habit of saving His people from armies they could never have beaten alone (Rom 8:31).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What are you currently measuring only by what you can count?
- How does it change things to remember God is not outnumbered?
- Where do you need to trust a promise instead of a headcount?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, my problems often look countless, and I feel small beside them. Remind me that You are never outnumbered and never overwhelmed. Amen.
